## Interpretations of Probability

Why do we model anything as random?  
What does "probability" mean in the real world?

1) <ins>Long-run frequency over repeated trials</ins>  
   $\underline{\text{Ex.}}$ repeatedly flipping a coin  
   shooting electrons at a double slit  
   "you can never step into the same river twice"

2) <ins>Systematic random sampling from a population</ins>  
   $\underline{\text{Ex.}}$ survey of 500 random voters  
   random assignment to treatment/control  
   Randomness comes from experimenter's actions

3) <ins>Subjective uncertainty about an outcome</ins>  
   chance that $\dots$
   * President Biden is re-elected
   * Higgs boson has a given mass
   * $\text{P} = \text{NP}$
   * $100^{\text{th}}$ digit of $\pi$ is 5  
   Could be broad intersubjective agreement

These are often intertwined:  
$\underline{\text{Ex.}}$ What if survey sampling is pseudo-random?  
Probably relying on shared ignorance

## Why not always be Bayesian?

$\underline{\text{Ex}}.\ X_1, \dots, X_n \overset{\text{iid}}{\sim} p$, $p$ unknown density on $\mathbb{R}$

$\underline{\text{Estimand}}:\quad m = \text{median}(p)$

$\underline{\text{Estimator}}\quad \delta(X) = \text{median}(X)$  
good estimator: robust, nonparametric  
large $n$: $\delta(X) \approx \mathcal{N}\left(m, (4np(m))^{-1}\right)$  
not Bayes for any realistic prior

<ins>Bayes approach</ins>  
$\underline{\text{Step 1}}.$ Define prior over $p$ (infinite-dim!)  
$\underline{\text{Step 2}}.$ Calculate posterior  
Horrific unless we pick special prior  
$\underline{\text{Step 3}}.$ Return e.g. $\mathbb{E}[m \mid X]$

If it differs substantially from $\text{median}(X)$,  
do we trust it?

## Where does $\Lambda$ come from?

(Bayesian rejoinder: Where does $\mathcal{P}$ come from?)

Four main sources for prior on $\Theta$

### <ins>Source #1: Subjective beliefs</ins>

$\underline{\text{Pro}}:$ Brings all relevant info. to bear  
Straightforward interp. of posterior

$\underline{\text{Con}}:$ Posterior is therefore subjective  
Embarrassing to write "I think" in abstract  
Hard if $\Theta$ high-dim or $\mathcal{P}$ nonparametric

$\underline{\text{Ex}}:$ Flip coin 20 times, get 7 heads  
0.5 probably a better estimate than 0.35  
My subjective prior on coins:

```
λ(θ)
 ^
 |          ||
 |          ||
 |          ||
 |          ||
 |          ||
 |_/\_______||_______/\_
 +----------+----------+--> θ
 0         0.5         1
```

## Source #2: "Objective" or "vague" prior

Using default prior removes subjectivity  
(But then what does the posterior mean?)

<ins>Flat prior</ins> $\quad \lambda(\theta) \propto_\theta 1 \quad \text{on } \Theta$  
"Indifference" (in $\theta$ parameterization)  
Often <ins>improper</ins> ($\Lambda(\Theta) = \infty$) but usually ok

$\underline{\text{Ex}}:\quad \theta \sim \text{flat prior on } \mathbb{R}$  
$X \mid \theta \sim \mathcal{N}(\theta, \sigma^2)$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lambda(\theta \mid x) &\propto_\theta p_\theta(x) \\
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-(x-\theta)^2 / 2\sigma^2} \\
&\propto_\theta \mathcal{N}(x, \sigma^2)
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Lambda([\theta, \theta + \varepsilon)) &\qquad (\text{Hw } 5) \\
&\approx \varepsilon \lambda(\theta) \propto \varepsilon \sqrt{J(\theta)} \\
&\approx \sqrt{D_{\text{KL}}(P_\theta \parallel P_{\theta+\varepsilon})}
\end{aligned}
$$

<ins>Jeffreys prior</ins> $\quad \lambda(\theta) \propto_\theta |J(\theta)|^{1/2}$  
Higher density where $P_\theta$ "changing faster"  
Invariant to parameterization

$\underline{\text{Ex}}.\quad X \mid \theta \sim \text{Binom}(n, \theta)$  
$\lambda(\theta) \propto_\theta J(\theta)^{1/2} = \left(\frac{n}{\theta(1-\theta)}\right)^{1/2} \propto_\theta \text{Beta}\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$

$\lambda(\theta) \to \infty \quad \text{as} \quad \theta \to 0 \text{ or } 1$:

$$
\underset{7n \cdot 10^{-3}}{D_{\text{KL}}(0.001 \parallel 0.01)} \overset{(33\times)}{\gg} \underset{2n \cdot 10^{-4}}{D_{\text{KL}}(0.49 \parallel 0.5)}
$$

```
λ(θ)
 |\_               _/|
 |  \             /  |
 |   \___________/   |
 +-------------------+-->
 0                   1   θ
```

## Intersubjective Agreement

Data may effectively rule out most $\theta$ values  
$\rightsquigarrow$ Makes posterior uncontroversial

$\underline{\text{Ex}}.\quad X \sim \text{Binom}(10^4, \theta)$, observe $X = 3000$

$$
\text{SD}_\theta(X/n) = \sqrt{\frac{\theta(1-\theta)}{n}} \le 0.005
$$

$$
\Rightarrow \text{Lik}(\theta; X) \approx 0 \quad \text{outside } C = [0.29, 0.31]
$$

All "reasonable" priors may be $\approx \text{flat}$ on $C$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \lambda(\theta \mid X) &\underset{\theta}{\approx} \text{Lik}(\theta; X) \\
&\underset{\theta}{\approx} \exp\left\{ -\frac{J(0.3)}{2} (\theta - 0.3)^2 \right\} \\
&\underset{\theta}{\propto} \mathcal{N}\left(0.3, J(0.3)^{-1}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

Data "swamps" everyone's prior

## Gaussian sequence model

$X \mid \theta \sim \mathcal{N}_d(\mu, I_d) \qquad \mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$

Jeffreys prior is flat: $\lambda(\mu) \underset{\mu}{\propto} 1$

$\lambda(\mu \mid x) = \mathcal{N}_d(X, I_d) \Rightarrow \mathbb{E}[\mu \mid X] = X$  
$\textcolor{red}{\text{Same as UMVU}}$

What about $\rho^2 = \|\mu\|^2$? Recall

$$
\mu \sim \mathcal{N}_d(X, I_d) \Rightarrow \mathbb{E}[\|\mu\|^2 \mid X] = \|X\|^2 + d
$$

Note $\delta_{\text{umvu}}(X) = \|X\|^2 - d \Rightarrow \delta_\lambda(X) = \delta_{\text{umvu}}(X) + 2d$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{MSE}(\theta; \delta_\lambda) &= \text{Var}_\theta(\delta_\lambda) + \text{Bias}_\theta(\delta_\lambda)^2 \\
&= \text{Var}_\theta(\delta_{\text{umvu}}) + 4d^2
\end{aligned}
$$

What went wrong? Examine Jeffreys prior:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{P}(\rho^2 \le t) &= \text{Vol}(\text{Ball of radius } \sqrt{t}) \\
&= \text{const}(d) \cdot t^{d/2} \\
\Rightarrow \lambda(\rho^2) &\underset{\rho^2}{\propto} (\rho^2)^{\frac{d}{2}-1} = \rho^{d-2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Grows rapidly! Prior "expects" $\rho^2$ to be huge

## Source #3: Prior or concurrent experience

May have many "copies" of same problem  
Assume corresp. $\Theta$ values drawn from a population  
$\rightsquigarrow$ Hierarchical Bayes / empirical Bayes  
Can be hard to choose right reference class

$\underline{\text{Ex}}.\quad \text{Estimate same-side bias for } m = 48 \text{ coin flippers}$  
Flipper $i$ has $n_i$ trials, "true" same-side prob $\theta_i$

$\underline{\text{Hierarchical model}}:\quad \text{flippers } i = 1, \dots, m$

$\textcolor{red}{\text{"hyperparameters"}}\ \alpha, \beta \sim \lambda \leftarrow \textcolor{red}{\text{"hyperprior"}}$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\theta_i \mid \alpha, \beta &\overset{\text{iid}}{\sim} \text{Beta}(\alpha, \beta) \\
X_i \mid \alpha, \beta, \theta &\overset{\text{ind.}}{\sim} \text{Binom}(n_i, \theta_i)
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\mathbb{E}[\theta_i \mid X, \alpha, \beta] = \frac{X_i + \alpha}{n_i + \alpha + \beta}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}[\theta_i \mid X] &= \mathbb{E}\left[ \mathbb{E}[\theta_i \mid X, \alpha, \beta] \mid X \right] \\
&= \iint \frac{X_i + \alpha}{n_i + \alpha + \beta} \lambda(\alpha, \beta \mid X) \, d\alpha \, d\beta
\end{aligned}
$$

If $m$ large $\alpha, \beta$ may be "almost known"  
$\rightsquigarrow$ choice of $\lambda$ doesn't matter much

## Flexibility of Bayes

Any $\Lambda$, $\mathcal{P}$, $L$, $g(\theta)$: $\delta_\Lambda$ defined straightforwardly

$$\delta_\Lambda(x) = \operatorname{argmin}_d \int L(\theta, d) \lambda(\theta | x) d\theta$$

Problem reduced to (possibly hard) computation  
Posterior is "one stop shop" for all answers

No need for:
- special family structure (exp. fam. / complete s.s.)
- special estimator (u-estimable)
- convex or nice $L$

$\Rightarrow$ Highly expressive modeling & estimation

<u>Caveat</u>: Limited by ability to do computations  
(Topic of next lecture)

## Source #4: Convenience Priors

Choosing conjugate or other "nice" priors  
$\rightsquigarrow$ much faster computations esp. in high-dim.  
(But what does the posterior mean?)
